A 37-year-old man arrives at the emergency department with a 3-day history of fever and headache.
He recently returned from a hiking trip in Tennessee and noticed red spots on his arms and legs upon
returning home, which he initially attributed to poison ivy. On examination, he has a macular petechial
rash on his trunk and extremities. His medical history includes atrial fibrillation managed with warfarin
and a penicillin allergy. He is started on the first-line antibiotic for his condition. What advice should be
provided to the patient regarding the medication he is most likely receiving? Answer Choices: (A) There
is about 10% chance that you will also be allergic to this medication (B) You may experience temporary
changes in taste sensation (C) Avoid drinking milk or taking antacids while you are on this medication
(D) Avoid direct sunlight while taking this medication (E) Your blood thinner levels may need to be
adjusted while on this medication (F) Take this medication with food to prevent stomach upset (G)
Avoid alcohol consumption while on this medication (H) Complete the full course even if symptoms
improve (I) Take this medication at bedtime to minimize side effects (J) This medication may cause
discoloration of your teeth
 A. You may experience temporary changes in taste sensation
B. Avoid alcohol consumption while on this medication
C. Complete the full course even if symptoms improve
D. This medication may cause discoloration of your teeth
E. Avoid drinking milk or taking antacids while you are on this medication

F. Avoid direct sunlight while taking this medication
G. There is about 10% chance that you will also be allergic to this medication
H. Take this medication with food to prevent stomach upset
I. Take this medication at bedtime to minimize side effects
J. Your blood thinner levels may need to be adjusted while on this medication
